CapCut vs VEXI: Video Editor or Social Media in One App?
CapCut is a capable video editor that you drive. VEXI edits the video for you, writes and designs the post, and posts it.
CapCut gives you the editing tools. Here is how it compares with one app that does the edit, the post and the posting for you.

CapCut is a video editor for phone, desktop and the web. It cuts, trims, adds transitions and auto-captions, and it has AI video and image generation and an AI design tool for social graphics. There is a no-cost tier; Pro is $19.99 a month. As an editor, it is very good, and a lot of people already know it.

VEXI (formerly Social Realtr) is an AI content studio that runs social media for entrepreneurs and creators. You describe what you want and it makes the posts, videos, designs and captions, then schedules and publishes them. Plans start at $199 a month, and every plan starts with a 15-day trial.

The difference is who does the editing. In CapCut you still sit at the timeline: you pick the clips, make the cuts, choose the music and fix the captions, then post it yourself. VEXI does the edit when you ask, writes the caption, and posts it. VEXI costs more than CapCut: plans are $199, $399 or $599 a month. What you pay for is the work you no longer do.
CapCut gives you the tools. Picking the clips, making the cuts and laying the music is still your time at the timeline.
VEXI edits the video for you: cuts, B-roll, music and captions. How deep the edit goes depends on your plan's mode, and anything you ask for wins.
CapCut's own guide covers sharing or scheduling to TikTok. For your other accounts you export and post somewhere else.
VEXI schedules and posts to your connected accounts itself.
CapCut opens when you open it. What to post, and when, is still yours to plan.
VEXI Autopilot runs your week ahead: it writes, cuts and posts, and can wait for your approval on everything.
CapCut's Trustpilot profile is rated 1.2. Some reviewers report charges they did not expect, a hard-to-find way to cancel, and support replies that go in circles.

Is CapCut enough to run my social media?
CapCut handles the edit if you do it yourself, and its own guide covers sharing or scheduling to TikTok. Writing the caption, planning the week and posting to your other accounts happen elsewhere.
For most posts, yes: VEXI edits the video for you with cuts, B-roll, music and captions, then posts it. If you love editing by hand, CapCut is a fine tool for that.
CapCut has a no-cost tier with basic tools. Pro is $19.99 a month on monthly billing, and the pricing page says prices can vary by region and offer.
